solved.topic: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string
solved.q: A string of length 0.5 m and mass per unit length 0.01 kg/m is stretched with a tension of 100 N. Find its fundamental frequency of vibration.
steps: Given: L = 0.5 m, m (mass/length) = 0.01 kg/m, T = 100 N.

solved.q: A stretched string of length 1 m has mass per unit length 0.01 kg/m under tension 64 N. Find (i) the fundamental frequency and (ii) the frequency of the third harmonic.
steps: Given: L = 1 m, m = 0.01 kg/m, T = 64 N.
Third harmonic frequency = 3 x n = 3 x 40.

solved.topic: Effect of tension change on string frequency
solved.q: A stretched string vibrates with a fundamental frequency of 300 Hz when the tension is 400 N. Find the new fundamental frequency if the tension is increased to 900 N, keeping length and mass per unit length unchanged.
steps: Since n is proportional to sqrt(T) (L, m constant): n2/n1 = sqrt(T2/T1).

solved.topic: Fundamental frequency of an open pipe
solved.q: Find the length of an open organ pipe whose fundamental frequency is 425 Hz. Take speed of sound in air as 340 m/s.
steps: Given: n = 425 Hz, v = 340 m/s, pipe is open at both ends.
Formula for open pipe: n = v/2L, so L = v/2n.

solved.topic: Fundamental frequency of a closed pipe
solved.q: A pipe closed at one end has length 0.25 m. Find its fundamental frequency of vibration. (speed of sound v = 340 m/s)
steps: Given: L = 0.25 m, v = 340 m/s, pipe closed at one end.
Formula for closed pipe: n = v/4L.

solved.topic: Length of closed pipe from a given harmonic
solved.q: The third harmonic of a closed organ pipe has a frequency of 510 Hz. Find the length of the pipe. (speed of sound v = 340 m/s)
steps: Given: closed pipe supports only odd harmonics n, 3n, 5n, ...; third harmonic frequency = 510 Hz.
Formula: n = v/4L, so L = v/4n.

solved.topic: Beat frequency of two tuning forks
solved.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. Find the beat frequency and the time interval between two successive beats.
steps: Time interval between successive beats = 1/(beat frequency) = 1/4.
Beat frequency = 4 Hz; time interval = 0.25 s.

solved.topic: Resonance tube method for speed of sound
solved.q: In a resonance tube experiment, the first and second resonance lengths of the air column are found to be 0.17 m and 0.52 m respectively, using a tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz. Find the speed of sound in air.
steps: Given: L1 = 0.17 m, L2 = 0.52 m, fork frequency n = 512 Hz.
Since successive resonances in a closed pipe occur at odd harmonics, L2 - L1 = lambda/2.
Formula: v = n x lambda = 2n(L2 - L1).

practice.q: A string of length 0.6 m and mass per unit length 0.004 kg/m is stretched with a tension of 90 N. Find its fundamental frequency.
A string has a fundamental frequency of 50 Hz. Find the frequency of its second overtone.
practice.hint: Second overtone is the third harmonic: frequency = 3n.

practice.q: Find the fundamental frequency of an open pipe of length 0.85 m. (v = 340 m/s)
practice.hint: Use n = v/2L for an open pipe.

practice.q: Find the length of a closed pipe whose fundamental frequency is 425 Hz. (v = 340 m/s)
practice.hint: Use n = v/4L for a closed pipe, solve for L.

practice.q: Two tuning forks produce 5 beats per second. If one fork has a frequency of 512 Hz, find the possible frequency of the other fork.
practice.hint: Beat frequency = |n1 - n2|; the unknown fork can be either n1 + 5 or n1 - 5.

practice.topic: Ratio of open and closed pipe fundamentals
practice.q: An open pipe and a closed pipe of the same length have fundamental frequencies n_open and n_closed. Find the ratio n_open : n_closed.
practice.hint: n_open = v/2L and n_closed = v/4L for the same L.
